details:
Terra Sonica is an interactive Earth Information Jukebox that turns NASA Earth observations into music you can hear and understand. It has five playable tracks, each sonifying a real dataset: global surface temperature from NASA GISTEMP (1880–2025, 146 yearly values), El Niño from Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomalies (2020–2026, 80 monthly values), active-fire detections across Brazil from NASA FIRMS/MODIS (2020–2025, 72 monthly counts), nighttime lights over India from NASA Black Marble/VIIRS (2012–2025, 14 yearly values), and Amazon tree cover from MODIS (2001–2024, 24 yearly values).

How it works: each observation becomes one note. The value is mapped to a pitch (220–880 Hz, snapped to E minor), so warmer, brighter, or more becomes higher. Every note shows its exact value, note name, and frequency, and "Explain My Sound" traces each note back to the observation behind it. A "Did You Hear That?" prompt on each track guides listeners to a real contrast — for example, the cold early 1900s against the hot 2020s — and the Forest track adds a two-year comparison and a listening check. Two tracks add a second data-driven voice (a fire-radiative-power drone on Fire, a growth voice on Sky), documented the same way.

Benefits and impact: it makes planetary change audible and intuitive, especially for blind and low-vision listeners and for anyone who learns better by listening than by reading a chart. It is built for accessibility — keyboard operable, screen-reader announcements, reduced-motion support — and every number is computed from the validated datasets, never invented.

Tools: React + TypeScript (Vite), Web Audio API, Vercel hosting, GitHub (public repo, MIT license), Google Earth Engine (geospatial processing of NASA MODIS tree-cover data). Data from NASA GISTEMP, NASA FIRMS, NASA Black Marble/VIIRS, NASA SVS, and MODIS; NOAA ERSSTv6 via the University of Miami. AI coding tools (Muse Code and Muse) assisted the build; the code is open.
